Header: Ceratitis cosyra, Bactrocera invadens, Dacus spp.

Prevention: Remove neglected/unmanaged host plants like guava, chillies, citrus, melons, coffee, mango and wild fruits to reduce potential hosts of fruit fly.
Prune timely and yearly to improve aeration.
Harvest ripe and mature green fruits regularly to reduce infestation levels as over-ripened fruits attract fruit flies.
Preserve natural enemies like ants, rove beetles, birds and parasitic wasps by planting hedge rows or wild flower strips of
Release poultry in the orchard to feed on pupa at the base of plants.
Monitoring: Regularly scout when fruit starts setting.
Look for pupae 2-5cm beneath host plant.
Look for adult fruit flies with 2 wings and a characteristic
Look out for premature fall of fruits that start to rot.
Monitor for fruits with oozing sap.
Look on fruit surfaces for small holes, punctured fruit, black lesions and soft spots.
Look inside fruit for rotting, maggots that jump on touch and discolouration.
Take action to control as soon as fruit flies and damage symptoms are observed on one plant.
Direct Control: Trap fruit flies using commercial traps when fruits start setting.

Remove infested fruits twice a week and destroy by burying about 2 feet deep, or tying in black plastic bag and leaving in sun for 3 days, or putting in boiling/hot water to kill larvae and then feed to poultry or pigs.
Flood around the base of trees with water weekly to kill pupae.
Keep harvested fruits in fully covered containers to prevent attack by fruit flies.
Store harvested fruit in a cool place or cold storage for 5 days.
Restrictions: PCPB for target crops and pests. www.pcpb.go.ke
Before use, read and follow pesticide product label instructions e.g
PHI, REI, usage and disposal of pesticide waste.
Do not empty pesticides into drains.
Always seek technical assistance before use of pesticide.
No synthetic pesticides registered against fruit fly in avocado.
Use pyrethrin-based products shortly after flowering.
